skills.name: Tambua na tumia vinyume vya vitenzi
skills.mastery: Gives the true opposite of a verb (kufunga-kufungua, kuvaa-kuvua, kuingia-kutoka) and does not use a negative form or a word of similar meaning, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Makes the opposite of a verb by adding si or ha (sifunga) instead of the opposite verb.
misconceptions.cause: The child takes "not doing it" to be the opposite.
misconceptions.reveals: An opposite question with a negative form as one option.
misconceptions.help: Is there one word that means the reverse action?
misconceptions.feedback: Kinyume cha kitenzi ni kitenzi kingine chenye maana ya kutengua kitendo, kama kufunga - kufungua. Si "kutofunga".
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Forms the opposite by adding -ua or -ulia to every verb (kuvaa to kuvaua).
misconceptions.cause: The child copies kufunga - kufungua for every verb.
misconceptions.reveals: An opposite where the pattern -ua does not work.
misconceptions.help: Say the word aloud: does it exist?
misconceptions.feedback: Vitenzi vingine vinabadilika kwa njia tofauti. Kinyume cha kuvaa ni kuvua.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a word of similar meaning instead of the opposite.
misconceptions.cause: The child keeps the same idea and does not reverse it.
misconceptions.reveals: An opposite question with a synonym as one option.
misconceptions.help: Does the word mean the same, or the other way round?
misconceptions.feedback: Kinyume kina maana ya upande wa pili. Kuingia na kutoka ni vinyume.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na tumia tashbihi za tabia
skills.mastery: Completes and picks a simile about behaviour (mkali kama simba, mwoga kama sungura) and does not leave out kama or take it word for word, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Gives the wrong animal or thing in the simile (mkali kama sungura).
misconceptions.cause: The child knows the idea but not the usual comparison.
misconceptions.reveals: A simile with plausible animals as options.
misconceptions.help: Which animal do we say is fierce?
misconceptions.feedback: Tashbihi hutumia ulinganisho wa kawaida: mkali kama simba, mwoga kama sungura, mpole kama kondoo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves out kama or "mithili ya", and says "Yeye ni simba" as a simile.
misconceptions.cause: The child mixes a simile with a metaphor.
misconceptions.reveals: A simile and a metaphor as options.
misconceptions.help: A simile has the word kama or mithili ya.
misconceptions.feedback: Tashbihi hulinganisha kwa kutumia kama au mithili ya: mkali kama simba. Kusema "yeye ni simba" ni sitiari.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes the simile word for word (the person is really a lion).

example.question: "Juma ni mwoga kama sungura" maana yake nini?

misconceptions.cause: The child does not read the comparison as a way to describe behaviour.
misconceptions.reveals: A meaning question for a simile.
misconceptions.help: Ask what behaviour the animal stands for.
misconceptions.feedback: Tashbihi inaelezea tabia kwa kulinganisha. "Mwoga kama sungura" ina maana mtu ana hofu sana.

skills.name: Tambua na tumia hali ya mazoea na hali timilifu
skills.mastery: Uses hu- for what is done every day (Juma hunywa maji) with no subject prefix, and -me- for what is finished (amemaliza), and does not mix them with -na- or -li-, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Adds a subject prefix to hu- (anahunywa, huanasoma).
misconceptions.cause: The child thinks every verb must have a person prefix.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap for hali ya mazoea with prefixed forms.
misconceptions.help: Say "Juma hunywa maji" aloud: does hu- already stand for the person?
misconceptions.feedback: Katika hali ya mazoea, hu- hubeba wakati na hakuna kiambishi cha mtu: Juma hunywa maji.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue influence on Kiswahili (to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher)

misconceptions.error: Uses -li- (past) where the action is complete and is still true now (-me-).
misconceptions.cause: The child treats -me- and -li- as the same: both mean "past".
misconceptions.reveals: A gap where the action is finished but still matters now.
misconceptions.help: Ask whether the action is finished now, with a result you can see.
misconceptions.feedback: -me- huonyesha kitendo kimekamilika na matokeo yake yapo sasa. -li- huonyesha kitendo cha zamani kilichopita.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses -na- (now) for what is done every day.
misconceptions.cause: The child thinks every action that happens "now" is -na-.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap for something done every week.
misconceptions.help: Does it happen every time, or only now?
misconceptions.feedback: Kitendo kinachofanyika kila mara huandikwa kwa hu-: Wanjiru hufua nguo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Kanusha viambishi vya nafsi na wakati
skills.mastery: Makes the negative of a verb in the present (-na-), past (-li-), perfect (-me-) and future (-ta-) for the persons ni-, u-, a-, tu-, m-, wa-, and does not only add si or keep the tense marker, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Makes the negative by putting si or hapana before the verb (si nasoma).
misconceptions.cause: The child copies English "I do not" or puts a word in front.
misconceptions.reveals: A negative with si before the verb.
misconceptions.help: Ask whether the verb itself changes its beginning.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitenzi kinakanushwa kwa kubadili kiambishi cha mtu na wakati ndani yake, si kwa kuweka "si" mbele. Ninasoma - sisomi.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue influence on Kiswahili (to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher)

misconceptions.error: Keeps the tense marker (-na-, -me-, -li-) in the negative (hamesoma instead of hajasoma).
misconceptions.cause: The child takes only the person prefix and keeps the rest.
misconceptions.reveals: A negative in -me- written as hame-.
misconceptions.help: Ask which letters replace -me- in the negative.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika ukanusho, -me- hubadilika kuwa -ja-: amesoma - hajasoma. -li- hubadilika kuwa -ku-: alisoma - hakusoma.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Keeps the positive person prefix (ni-, tu-, wa-) in the negative.
misconceptions.cause: The child changes the tense but not the person prefix.
misconceptions.reveals: A negative of tu- written as tu- plus si.
misconceptions.help: Ask what the negative of ninasoma starts with (si-), and of tutasoma (hatu-).
misconceptions.feedback: Viambishi vya nafsi hubadilika katika ukanusho: ni- - si-, u- - hu-, a- - ha-, tu- - hatu-, m- - ham-, wa- - hawa-.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Keeps -na- in the negative present (hasomina, hanasoma).
misconceptions.cause: The child drops -na- but not entirely; present negative has no tense marker.
misconceptions.reveals: A negative present with -na- kept.
misconceptions.help: Say the negative aloud: does it have -na-?
misconceptions.feedback: Wakati uliopo hukanushwa bila -na-, na kitenzi humalizika kwa -i: anasoma - hasomi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives the negative of another tense (hasomi for hajasoma, sikusoma for sisomi).
misconceptions.cause: The child makes a correct negative but of the wrong tense.
misconceptions.reveals: A negative of a different tense among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask which tense the positive sentence is in, and which negative marks it.
misconceptions.feedback: Ukanusho wa kila wakati una kiambishi chake: -na- hukanushwa bila kiambishi (hasomi), -me- huwa -ja- (hajasoma), -li- huwa -ku- (hakusoma), -ta- hubaki -ta- (hatasoma).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Badilisha nomino za m- kuwa ukubwa na udogo
skills.mastery: Gives the big form (ji-) and the small form (ki-) of nouns that begin with m- (mtoto: jitoto, kitoto; mti: jiti, kijiti; mji: jiji, kijiji), and uses them in a sentence, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.
Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Swaps the big form (ji-) and the small form (ki-).
misconceptions.cause: The child learned both prefixes but not which means big and which small.
misconceptions.reveals: Questions that ask for big and for small.
misconceptions.help: Ki- is the prefix of kijiji, kitoto, kijiko: small things.
misconceptions.feedback: Ki- huonyesha udogo (kitoto, kijiji) na ji- huonyesha ukubwa (jitoto, jiji).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Keeps the m- (jimtoto, kimtoto) when the new prefix goes on.
misconceptions.cause: The child adds the prefix to the whole word.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap where m- is left on.
misconceptions.help: Take away the m- of mtoto, then add ji-.
misconceptions.feedback: M- ya mwanzo huondolewa kabla ya kuongeza kiambishi cha ukubwa au udogo: mtoto - jitoto, kitoto.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Does not add ji- to a noun with one-syllable root (mti, mto, mji) when making the small form (kimti, kimto).
misconceptions.cause: The child uses the rule for longer roots.
misconceptions.reveals: Small forms of mji, mto, mti.
misconceptions.help: Say the word kijiji aloud: where is the ji?
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino zenye shina la silabi moja zinaongeza ji- kabla ya ki-: mji - kijiji, mto - kijito, mti - kijiti.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Badilisha nomino za n- kuwa ukubwa na udogo
skills.mastery: Gives the big form and the small form of nouns that begin with n- (nyumba: jumba, kijumba; mbwa: jibwa, kibwa), and uses them in a sentence, in 8 of 10 new items.

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher.

misconceptions.error: Keeps the n- or ny- of the noun (jinyumba, kinyumba).
misconceptions.cause: The child does not drop the first sound as with m- nouns.
misconceptions.reveals: A gap where the first sound is kept.
misconceptions.help: Say "jumba la ghorofa", not "jinyumba".
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino za n- hubadilika kwa kuondoa sauti ya mwanzo: nyumba - jumba, kijumba. Baadhi huongeza ji- (mbwa - jibwa).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Swaps ji-/ju- (big) and ki- (small) for n- nouns.
misconceptions.cause: Two prefixes and two meanings, learned together.
misconceptions.reveals: Big and small forms asked in turn.
misconceptions.help: Ki- is small: kijumba is a hut.
misconceptions.feedback: Ki- huonyesha udogo: kijumba. Ukubwa huonyeshwa na ji- au umbo la pekee kama jumba.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher
